title: Cristiano Ronaldo at least omitted the ‘say something like’ part
trail: In today’s Fiver: Ronnie, Santiago Muñez comes to life and Moira Rose
body: THE SIXER! The Fiver was entirely unsurprised by the self-congratulation emanating from Old Trafford on Tuesday, its smugness even more intense than usual. “Ronaldo is coming home,” tooted Manchester United’s website, handily ignoring the fact that the player in question spent the final year of his first spell at the club in a flounce, whinging that the privilege of donning the famous red shirt made him feel like a “slave”, before binning the Reds to spend the peak of his career in white at Real Madrid. United then did the honourable thing, honouring his legacy by replacing Ronnie with Antonio Valencia, Gabriel Obertan and Michael Owen, before largely pocketing the rest of the Portuguese’s world record transfer fee. In his own statement on Social Media Disgrace Instagram, Ronaldo at least omitted the “Say something like ...” part of the line he was presumably told to publish by his Mr 15%, telling us that he’s been “overwhelmed by all the messages” sent to him since the deal was announced on Friday. Course he was. “This is absolutely 100% the stuff that dreams are made of!,” Ronnie nostalgia-ed. “My first domestic League, my first Cup, my first call to the Portuguese National team, my first Champions League, my first Golden Boot and my first Ballon d’Or, they were all born from this special connection between me and the Red Devils. History has been written in the past and history will be written once again! You have my word! … PS – Sir Alex, this one is for you”. As opposed to the 2009-10 league title, for example. Ole Gunnar Solskjær was also ready with his hosannahs, enthusing that Ronaldo is “coming home to where it all started”, because Sporting Clube de Portugal are but an inconvenient truth. “You run out of words to describe Cristiano”, Solskjær described, words that dripped with candour when he immediately deployed some new ones, informing us that Ronaldo is “not only a marvellous player but a great human being”. Ok, Ole! LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE Niall McVeigh has donned his yellow tie and set up in our concrete-reinforced transfer bunker to bring your all the latest deadline-day thrills and spills in our liveblog. If you prefer your transfers more bulletpointy, catch up with the latest moves in our women’s and men’s transfer interactives. QUOTE OF THE DAY “The dream begins” – Newcastle United make reference to the infamous 2005 film, Goal! – in which protagonist Santiago Muñez, played by Kuno Becker, makes it big at St James’ Park – in their deadline-day announcement to sign Mexico Under-23 striker Santiago Muñóz. FIVER LETTERS “At first glance I wasn’t sure how the story of Keith the Duck getting a minute’s applause at Wigan Athletic this weekend was related to football, but the more I think about it, the more I realise that it fits the bill” – James Vortkamp-Tong. “Yes Barry, “hapless” is certainly the word for you. Any slight chance to try & put the boot in to Utd [re Friday’s Fiver], you’re in the queue, slavering with anticipation. You are a disgrace to any fair journalism. Your bitterness disgusts me. Get a life!” – Steve Thomas. “Villarreal v Atlético Madrid this weekend was proof that you can take a man out of Arsenal but never the Arsenal out of the man” – krishnamoorthy. Send your letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. And you can always tweet The Fiver via @guardian_sport. Today’s winner of our prizeless letter o’ the day is … Steve Thomas. RECOMMENDED VIEWING Three minutes of pure video pleasure, as we mop up the best transfer announcements of the summer, with efforts inspired by Home Alone, Grand Theft Auto and Fresh Prince of Bel Air. Includes this one of course … you beauty! NEWS, BITS AND BOBS Troy Deeney has admitted to feeling proud but glum after he exited Vicarage Road for Birmingham. “I feel sadness and a loss similar to losing a family member,” parped the forward. Nikola Vlasic is a West Ham player after David Moyes opted against pursuing Jesse Lingard and instead threw £25.7m to CSKA Moscow. Manchester City are confident of beating Real Madrid Femenino despite being without Lucy Bronze and Ellen White for tonight’s Women’s Big Cup qualifier first leg. “People might think that, because of their name, Real are an experienced team but they’re not,” scoffed new signing Vicky Losada, formerly of Barça. Brighton have given Getafe some of their Ben White moolah in adding Spain international Marc Cucurella to their summer acquisitions. Moise Kean’s Mersey dream may be nearing an end with his loan move to Juve confirmed on Tuesday morning. ICYMI because bank holiday: Ainsley Maitland-Niles asked to leave Arsenal via Instagram yesterday. “All I want to do is go where I’m wanted & where I’m going to play @Arsenal,” he sadtromboned. In (potentially) happier news for the Gunners, they have agreed a £17m deal for Bologna defender Takehiro Tomiyasu. RECOMMENDED LOOKING It’s ya boy, David Squires, on a remarkable transfer window. Like this cartoon? You can buy it right here in our print shop. STILL WANT MORE? What does Lionel Messi’s arrival at PSG mean for Kylian Mbappé? Being perma-tinkered with and the subject of relentless future transfer chat, reckons Eric Devin. Deals for Ronaldo and Romelu Lukaku show that fans’ need for new signings outstrips thirst for change, laments Jonathan Liew. Juventus look lost as their post-Ronaldo era begins with embarrassment by Empoli, uh-ohs Nicky Bandini. Köln give their fans reason to believe again after seasons of struggle, fistpumps Andy Brassell. The first half-dozen WSL previews are in: for Arsenal, Aston Villa, Birmingham, Brighton, Chelsea and Everton. Unai Emery loses the plot after Atlético snatched a draw with Villarreal thanks to a comedy own goal, thigh-slaps Sid Lowe. Finally, it’s Last Mill Of The Window time, aka The One Where Everything’s Soon To Be Proven Wrong. And sign up for a daily Big Sports Day email here.
